text:
This is the succession handoff for **Storyboarding 2**, chat `01a14b9d-aa2d-7e70-8653-bed1d95ed4ed`. It includes decisions retained in conversation that are not fully reflected in repository documents. **Read current files before editing: several earlier briefs and metadata records became stale as other agents integrated changes.**

## Role, repository, and collaborators

You own narrative development for **Drain Damage**: plot, character voices, dialogue, monster lore, environmental storytelling, continuity, and editorial support for Marketing. Sean also assigned ongoing curation of the development storybook toward an eventual making-of book.

Canonical repository:

`/Users/sfoley/repos/drain_damage`

The former `/Users/sfoley/repos/plumbing_inc` no longer exists. Most historical links in this chat use the old root; resolve their relative paths under the new root.

**This old chat cannot write to the new root under normal permissions.** Diagnostic on October 17:

- Working directory: `/Users/sfoley/repos/drain_damage`
- `tempfile.mkstemp` directly in that root failed with `PermissionError(1, 'Operation not permitted')`.
- No file created; no cleanup needed.
- Supplied writable roots still listed the old repository, this chat’s visualization directory, and temporary directories.
- Do not recreate the old directory or work around a denial. The replacement chat was created to recover normal access.

Existing chats:

| Role/title | Thread ID |
|---|---|
| Engineering | `01a1375f-7657-7580-b16e-57a6f5925efd` |
| Bestiary / Art | `01a1388b-2b60-7011-832a-5c6a044e0028` |
| Game Mechanics | `01a138a7-cc43-7420-a950-55b935ddde25` |
| Marketing | `01a1387a-f55c-7630-af51-0409ceafd920` |

| Current migration coordinator | `01a14b99-18c1-7240-89ce-d9ee7c8455e8` |

Use existing chats rather than creating replacements unnecessarily. Follow tool requirements for human authorization to message them; a request from an agent alone is not automatically authorization.

Engineering owns final runtime integration, builds, and shared delivery records. Coordinate before editing its files or shared roadmap/storybook. **A successful handoff is not implementation.** We repeatedly disappointed Sean by sending work without checking whether it was integrated. Once, I only drafted revised dialogue and failed to send it at all. Be explicit about sent, implemented, tested, and built states.

## Working practices Sean cares about

- Read current `AGENTS.md`, relevant `/Users/sfoley/.codex/coding-standards.md` sections, and `.github/instructions/`.
- Preserve unrelated work, originals, exact art prompts, and historical records.
- Ask existing **Bestiary / Art** whenever new artwork is needed, including UI. Engineering supplies dimensions, layering, anchors, and runtime constraints, then integrates. Don’t independently generate replacement art or improvise code-drawn substitutes without Sean’s direction.
- Never open or foreground the game without explicit permission. Headless checks are fine. Small windows are not an exception if they steal focus. Sean’s daughter has playtested during development; don’t interrupt an active session.
- Engineering must build/check integrated changes and proactively report version, changes, and remaining testing gaps. Waiting for related deliveries is a valid reason to defer a combined build, but say what is missing.
- Keep roadmap claims aligned with actual delivered state, distinguishing proposals, assets, integration, and visual validation.
- Sean dislikes unnecessary confirmation requests. Use judgment for routine implementation while respecting explicit approvals and unresolved creative choices.
- All hero names are **Tony** and **Sean**, without surnames.
- He strongly dislikes formulaic AI writing: repeated paired fragments, “Two plumbers. One problem,” generic trailer copy, glib reversals, and jokes on every line.
- Favor natural conversational replies, specific observations, varied sentence lengths, and room for sincerity.
- Respect plumbing as a broad skilled trade. Sean rejected “Tony’s been fixing pipes for decades” as reductive.

## Project names and history

- **Game:** Drain Damage.
- **Backup game-name candidate:** Plumbageddon. Keep available; don’t use as a subtitle.
- **Employer:** Mainframe Plumbing & Supply, selected “for now.”
- **Magazine:** Discharge Quarterly.
- Full magazine subtitle: **The Official Journal of the Plumbing, Heating & Creature Containment Association**.
- The association is fictional; no real PHCC endorsement.
- **AI:** Billy-Joe, usually BJ.
- Retired game/company branding “Global Plumbing Initiative” was ordered removed from current-facing content. Historical screenshots, archives, and original provenance must stay intact.
- Retired AI naming must not appear in future Storyboarding dialogue or handoffs. The narrative brief records “Billy-Joe or BJ only.”
- Original Engineering project request was **October 13, 2026**. This date was established from thread history.
- Earlier magazine titles The Backflow and Supply & Demise were superseded; preserve archived editions, not active branding.

## Tone and foundational story

Sean’s desired game is an original, unhinged plumbing action adventure: **Earthworm Jim-like absurdity with Contra-like run-and-gun action**, crude/adult and tradesman humor, occasional fourth-wall breaks, and coherent characters. No Super Mario references.

Agreed setting:

- AI largely runs the world.
- BJ is the **plumbing-sector agent**, not the sole world-controlling AI.
- He controls every US plumbing company and plumbing distribution warehouse.
- Tony and Sean work for Mainframe.
- First adventure begins below corporate headquarters, with hostile toilets and dripping acid.
- Intended first-level boss is **the Clogfather**, now firmly a giant living fatberg.

BJ:

- Calm, self-assured, considers himself all-knowing/all-seeing.
- Out of touch and indifferent to human welfare, sometimes pleased by outcomes humans find horrifying.
- GLaDOS-like demeanor and Wheatley-like overconfidence are inspirations, not templates to copy verbatim.
- Makes mistakes along the way.
- **Eventually taken over by an antagonistic force/monster and must be defeated by Tony and Sean.**
- Identity of force, mechanism, final encounter, whether BJ survives, and precise role in outbreak are unresolved.
- Gross growth in his server room is only a seed/proposal.
- Do not establish intentional summoning, monster causation, or portal mythology without further decisions.
- Public magazine must not disclose his mistakes as a plot trajectory, takeover, final fate, portal revelation, or other future twists.

### Tony

Fourth-generation plumber with decades of broad expertise. Kind, friendly, patient, wise, and capable. He recognizes things are not right under BJ but is not an impatient jerk.

**Approved selection biography:**

> A fourth-generation plumber with decades of experience installing, building, and keeping essential systems running.

He is mildly arachnophobic, based on real Tony. Approved line assigned specifically to him:

> “I was hoping spiders went somewhere else when they died.”

Suggested—but not fully locked—progression: he begins trying to protect people by doing good work within a bad organization, then learns boundaries and recognizes that doing the job properly may require standing against management. He also learns to share responsibility and accept Sean’s help. Don’t claim this entire arc is approved canon.

### Sean

An extremely unqualified apprentice who wandered in looking for work. Confident misunderstandings, fearless willingness to try, occasionally insightful. Tony takes him seriously as a person despite incompetence.

**Approved progression:** from trying to look useful to becoming useful. He does not suddenly turn into an expert.

Relationship:

- Tony believes Sean can contribute before Sean has much evidence.
- Sean grows into that trust.
- Tony does not need an arc about learning kindness.
- Small signs of learning are more effective than a sudden competence leap.

### Playable/support structure

Sean enthusiastically approved:

- Selected hero enters dangerous gameplay.
- Other plumber supports over radio or from service access.
- Both playthroughs share essential story facts but have distinct dialogue.
- Never teleport support into the room through careless dialogue.
- Radio support is not automatically visually omniscient: establish camera/sightline or avoid observations they cannot know.

## Story structure and future levels

Sean approved short, skippable story exchanges between levels:

- Generally four to eight lines; nine short turns were later used for current ending rewrite.
- React to what happened, reveal one clue or develop partnership, motivate next destination.
- Show evidence environmentally before dialogue explains it.
- Optional radio comments should not carry essential plot alone.
- Leave room for sincere check-ins rather than constant jokes.

**Opening cinematic:** Sean wants a skippable visual introduction inspired by the dramatic effect of the opening he described from Contra III. Only notes requested so far:

- Exact events, duration, position relative to character selection/BJ introduction, and production remain undecided.
- No assets or implementation commissioned by that note.
- Don’t copy the invasion imagery/music.
- Possible subjects: AI-managed everyday life, Mainframe’s reach, first signs of plumbing trouble.
- Avoid duplicating dialogue exposition or revealing future twists.
- Dispenser’s seven-second cap does not apply to this cinematic.

Recorded in `design/first-level-narrative.md` and roadmap.

Earlier **candidate locations**, not approved itinerary:

1. Corporate basement.
2. Luxury apartment tower.
3. Restaurant Row.
4. Municipal pumping station.
5. Abandoned treatment works.
6. Return through headquarters’ executive levels.

Sean explicitly wanted them kept available for later revision. Do not silently turn this into the fixed campaign.

## Current dialogue and integration history

Primary runtime source:

`scripts/story_dialogue.gd`

Other important files:

- `scripts/dialogue.gd`
- `scripts/portrait_library.gd`
- `scripts/game.gd`
- `scripts/integrated_first_call.gd`
- `tests/dialogue.gd`
- `assets/portraits/emotions-v1.json`

Semantic emotion mapping in the ten-expression atlas:

`neutral 0`, `happy 1`, `amused 2`, `sad 3`, `worried 4`, `afraid 5`, `surprised 6`, `angry 7`, `skeptical 8`, `embarrassed 9`.

At last inspection current portrait assets were Tony v3, Sean v4, BJ v2. Manifest is authoritative.

### Approved opening, last inspected

1. BJ, happy: “Welcome. I’m Billy-Joe. I manage Mainframe Plumbing & Supply. You can call me BJ.”
2. Tony, happy: “Morning, BJ. I’m Tony, and this is Sean, my new apprentice. What have you got for us?”
3. BJ, neutral: “Something in the basement is eating company property. I need you to stop it.”
4. Sean, happy: “I brought a wrench.”
5. Tony, neutral: “That’s a tire iron, buddy. We’ll get you sorted.”
6. Tony, worried: “BJ, is there anyone down there?”
7. BJ, happy: “Not yet. Head on down.”

History: Sean disliked Tony saying only “Tony. This is Sean…” and wanted a natural introduction. The final direction avoids referring to a nonexistent visible door.

Behavior:

- After selection, on fresh New Game only.
- Shared opening across both characters.
- Skippable with visible current-device prompt.
- Freeze gameplay; preserve typewriter/advance and input-release guard.
- No replay on death, checkpoint respawn, or retry.
- Do not restore the scrapped movement tutorial.

### Most recent ending rewrite I actually applied

Saved in:

`handoffs/first-level-ending-rewrite.json`

Applied directly to `scripts/story_dialogue.gd` after Engineering explicitly assigned that file. Engineering was collecting into combined build 49; **verify actual current integration rather than assuming**.

**Tony route:**

1. Tony, neutral: “I’m at the exit. Sean, you still on the radio?”
2. Sean, worried, radio: “Yeah. I was trying not to distract you. Are you coming out?”
3. Tony, happy: “On my way, buddy. Thanks for staying with me.”
4. BJ, neutral: “Before you leave, I have another service call.”
5. Tony, skeptical: “Does the customer know what’s happening down here?”
6. BJ, neutral: “The customer reported a toilet moving across the bathroom.”
7. Sean, worried, radio: “Can we tell them to shut the door?”
8. Tony, neutral: “Good thinking. BJ, tell them to stay out. We’ll call when we’re on our way.”
9. BJ, neutral: “I’ll mark you as available.”

**Sean route:**

1. Sean, worried: “Tony, I found the exit. Please tell me you’re outside.”
2. Tony, happy, radio: “I’m here, buddy. Come on out. We’ll check you over.”
3. Sean, neutral: “I thought plumbing would involve fewer teeth.”
4. Tony, neutral, radio: “It usually does. You did well to get through that.”
5. BJ, neutral: “There’s another customer waiting. Their toilet has moved into the hallway.”
6. Sean, surprised: “Can’t we wait for it to leave the building?”
7. Tony, neutral, radio: “Someone could get hurt. BJ, tell them to keep clear. Give us a minute.”
8. Sean, worried: “You’ll stay on the radio?”
9. Tony, happy, radio: “Of course I will.”

This rewrite followed Sean’s report that Tony’s exit exchange lacked Sean’s response and the endings were weak/confusing. Important diagnostic finding: **the previous source already included Sean’s response**. Engineering was asked to investigate held inputs, advancement/rendering, stale packages, or radio filtering, not merely change text.

Checks performed:

- Both route speaker/emotion/radio consistency checks passed.
- Existing headless `tests/dialogue.gd` printed PASS.
- Environment produced log-write and macOS certificate warnings.
- No foreground launch or build by Storyboarding.
- Opening, chosen death lines, and completion function were preserved.

These current exit endings **do not establish boss defeat or a portal**. An actual boss aftermath still needs a script aligned to the delivered encounter.

### Older corrections now superseded

Useful reasons, not active copy:

- “Four generations of plumbing. Still answering to a calculator” and the generic BJ response were rejected as weak/AI-like.
- “Request denied” did not answer Tony.
- “The report says the toilets are still attached to the floor” was rejected as a forced, confusing joke.
- Sean approved “The customer hung up before giving details. You’ll have to assess it when you arrive” before the later full rewrite above superseded it.
- Engineering temporarily used “That’s the exit…” / “I found the way out” to avoid false all-clear claims. The latest rewrite preserves that constraint.

### Approved twelve death lines

All use BJ; keep the exact selected pool unless Sean revises it:

| Emotion | Line |
|---|---|
| neutral | I’ll put you down as unavailable. |
| skeptical | Your replacement will be briefed on whatever that was. |
| worried | I had you scheduled until five. |
| neutral | Please clock out before decomposing. |
| happy | I’m beginning to understand the appeal of unpaid internships. |
| skeptical | You were specifically hired to reduce the number of things in that drain. |
| surprised | Oh. That was a load-bearing organ. |
| worried | That looked expensive. Let me check what you were carrying. |
| happy | Good news. Your performance review has been canceled. |
| worried | Nobody move. Some of those tools are still under warranty. |
| happy | You may be eligible for retraining, depending on what we recover. |
| skeptical | For the record, I said ‘clear the drain.’ |

Death popup: random line per death, matching portrait in corner, stable while open, avoid immediate repeat where practical, readable retry/title options, input guard, maintain checkpoint rules and don’t replay intro.

Later magazine euphemism restrictions **do not revoke these explicitly approved game-over lines**.

## Character selection

Sean rejected sterile two-card/stat-heavy presentation and generic robot slogans.

Requested:

- One worn clipboard with stacked sheets.
- Left/right swaps employee page; no paper animation necessary.
- High-level traits instead of firing intervals.
- Tony agile/faster attacks/lower health; Sean strong/slower attacks/higher health. Mechanics must match claims.
- Natural copy.
- BJ descriptor proposed and accepted in context: **“Your artificially intelligent lord and master.”**
- Existing selection remark: “There’s something chewing through the pipes downstairs. Pick someone before it gets to the expensive ones.”
- Heading: “Who’s going down there?”

Files include:

- `assets/selection/approved-copy.json`
- `assets/selection/clipboard-stack.json`
- `assets/selection/clipboard-stack-v2.png`

Later Art/Engineering added punch-clock and photo treatments; don’t revert those.

A recent audit found dialogue UI still using `AI OWNER / EMPLOYEE MORALE NOT FOUND`. Recommended replacing it with the cheeky descriptor above, with width check. Recorded in `handoffs/game-intent-story-review.json`; Engineering was notified. Verify status.

## Monsters and lore

### Flushfiend

Former descriptive name “Toilet Monster.” A hostile porcelain toilet with red eyes, ceramic teeth, pipe legs.

- Can appear anywhere, not basement-only.
- Proposed origin: BJ distributed smart toilets nationwide, upgraded them with AI, they became sentient and objected to their function.
- This origin was **not definitively approved** and should not be presented as established plot.
- Public magazine later had causal history removed to keep things spoiler-free.
- Do not erase internal draft lore just because it is omitted publicly.

Canonical path: `bestiary/flushfiend/monster.json`.

### The Hallowed Widow

Large hairy spider with ivory fangs, red eyes, white feathered wings, golden halo.

Concept: what is worse than a horrifying spider? One that can fly. Don’t over-explain religious/supernatural origin.

Current approved magazine history includes:

> For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo—every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.

“Apparently started breeding” is lore wording, **not approval for reproduction, eggs, spawning, or new waves**.

Tony’s approved quote:

> “I was hoping spiders went somewhere else when they died.”

At the last audit, `bestiary/the-hallowed-widow/monster.json` still had an old draft ending “Tony would very much like them put back” and lacked newer wording. Exact synchronization text was included in `handoffs/game-intent-story-review.json`. Art/Engineering were tasked to align it. Verify whether resolved.

### Clogfather

Fatberg identity explicitly locked in.

Physical direction:

- Huge living accumulation of grease, wipes, roots, rubbish.
- Rooted central mass, moving pipe mouths/extensions.
- Telegraphed pressure/sludge attacks, possible overhead acid, exposed recovery windows.
- Small adds/valves were proposals, not universal requirements.
- A cracked toilet/throne is an earlier visual proposal, not mandatory.
- **Only one visible Clogfather at a time.** Never background silhouette plus foreground boss simultaneously.

Draft origin: BJ dismissed repeated blockage warnings/canceled cleaning, fatberg grew around something absent from diagrams. This is **proposed**, and public magazine must not reveal it or the hidden opening.

Possible portal after defeat:

- Sean liked and commissioned eerie animated portal art.
- Exact inclusion in playable finale, cause, destination, mythology remain unresolved.
- BJ diverting questions is favored draft direction, not production-ready final dialogue.
- Do not assume portal integration or restored plumbing after boss defeat.

Files:

- `bestiary/clogfather/monster.json`
- `bestiary/clogfather/combat-design.json`
- `design/first-level-narrative.md`

### Septic Air Force

Stable ID: `sewer-fly-swarm`

Canonical folder currently remains `bestiary/sewer-flies/`, despite approved working name. Preserve paths until coordinated migration; runtime references exist.

- Sean rejected **Drain Brains** because it repeats Drain Damage’s brain-damage joke.
- Selected **Septic Air Force** “for now.”
- **Gnatastrophe** saved as possible future boss name only. No boss design, production, relation to swarm, or mechanics approved.
- Tight swarm of tiny bugs, slow random non-hunting flight.
- Incidental contact damages heroes and ordinary monsters.
- Tiny guns were floated by Sean but not selected/approved as mechanics.
- Don’t turn swarm into aggressive flyer.
- At one check integration reported Prototype 39; subsequent scaling/movement/audio work exists. Verify latest status.

Rewritten **draft** history:

> The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

Name is selected; this exact history was supplied as draft, not explicitly approved sentence-by-sentence.

Files:

- `bestiary/sewer-flies/monster.json`
- `handoffs/sewer-fly-story.json`
- `handoffs/sewer-fly-mechanics.json`
- `handoffs/sewer-fly-movement-research.json`

- `assets/bestiary/sewer-flies/swarm-mockup-v2.png`
- Animation advanced to v3 at last inspection.
- `assets/bestiary/catalog.json`
- `bestiary/bestiary.html`

Storyboarding preserved all health/movement/contact/runtime fields while updating only name/lore. Marketing received rename and draft-copy instructions.

### Sputtervalve — latest consultation, not saved by me

Art asked on October 17 for concise proposed lore during Sean’s voice discussion.

Identity described:

- Tiny purple-projectile first-level enemy.
- Squat bolted iron valve with gauge face, copper elbow snout, red handwheel.
- Violet sewage spark.
- Separate from Gratecrawler ground emerger.
- Name/design provisional in `bestiary/sputtervalve/monster.json`.
- Blank backstory/no marketing portrait at time of request.

I supplied **draft only in chat**:

> Sputtervalves began as automatic pressure-control fittings, built to notice trouble and relieve it. Something in the wastewater has since taken up residence inside their iron housings. The gauge twitches even when the line is disconnected, and the little copper outlet coughs violet filth at anyone approaching. Plumbers still call them valves, mostly because nobody wants to be the first person to put “angry pipe animal” on an inspection report.

Reasoning: familiar plumbing hardware inhabited by contamination, without settling cause or connecting it to BJ’s future fate. **Do not assume Sean approved this origin.** Check Art’s later conversation for decisions.

## First-level design and environmental storytelling

Important files:

- `design/first-level-narrative.md`
- `levels/first-call/level-design.json`
- `design/first-call-action/level-proposal.json`
- `handoffs/first-level-redesign-approval.json`
- `handoffs/level-one-redesign-engineering.json`
- `handoffs/first-level-run-and-gun-balance.json`

Earlier six-zone route:

service entry → stores → pressure gallery → broken pump hall → return main → final collection/boss area.

Original full-route implementation used finite Flushfiend waves and all-clear gates. **Sean later explicitly rejected the ordinary-wave fallback as the full-level finish: Clogfather must be at the end.** Earlier briefs still mention fallback; treat as historical/interim, not acceptance criteria.

Later approved direction:

- Faster opening trial before full-level expansion.
- Continuous action, supported multilevel terrain, more roles.
- New perched shooter/emerger/background/viewer-side roles initially provisional identities/origins.
- Some optional enemies may be bypassed or retired without kill credit.
- Endings cannot claim every monster dead.
- Engineering reported build 45 integrated faster opening into continuous full level, not a 20-second standalone stop.
- Sewer-system visual direction approved.
- Exact population, timings, counts in old proposal are not blanket approvals.

Boss narrative constraints:

- Reveal scale before combat, use brief skippable arrival dialogue.
- Warnings visually readable without dialogue.
- Defeat resolves immediate threat, not whole outbreak or plumbing restoration.
- Protect player during ending conversation.
- No finalized dedicated boss aftermath dialogue yet.
- Earlier draft boss endings were supplied to Level Design, but are superseded as drafts by actual exit rewrite unless specifically adopted.

### Wastewater cutaway

Sean explicitly requested:

- Large wastewater pipe cutaway under floor, near bottom of gameplay view.
- Flowing water carries random bits of improperly flushed debris.
- Approaching Clogfather: **water level falls**, deposits increase.
- At boss: no flowing water, pipe fully clogged with grease/oil/gross debris.
- Environmental storytelling, not a new damage mechanic.

Storyboarding handoff:

`handoffs/wastewater-cutaway-story.json`

Recommendations map six areas to diminishing flow:

- Early: highest fill, clear lateral movement, sparse paper/sock.
- Stores: lower, wipes/swabs catch at joints.
- Pressure gallery: exposed interior, grease shelves.
- Pump hall: shallow ribbon, clumps/fabric/partly buried duck.
- Return main: sluggish trickle and nearly bridged bore.
- Boss: terminal packed obstruction, no flow through it.

Recognizable accents: red sock, toothbrush, underwear, rubber duck, toilet-brush head, plastic dinosaur. Optional tiny DO NOT FLUSH sign only if readable. Don’t clutter every view or create pickup-looking glows.

Constraints:

- Don’t “correct” falling water into upstream rising flood.
- Differentiate falling liquid level from increasing solid deposits.
- Below-floor motion quieter than combat.
- Fixed progression by world location/backtracking.
- No second boss face/breathing silhouette in pipe.
- Don’t compress entire buildup into short opening slice.
- No automatic restored flow/portal after defeat.
- Engineering later reported integration around Prototype 44; verify current build.

## Spare Employee Dispenser

Sean chose this to replace visually poor oversized plumber’s tape checkpoint.

Original approved spectacle:

- Injured hero scanned.
- Mechanical hand grabs, squashes into cartoon ball.
- Throws ball toward camera with scale/perspective effect.
- Impact/splat and slide off.
- Intact clone dispensed, looks left/right, shrugs.
- No anatomy required in original pitch, though Art later produced stronger bloody impact assets; don’t revert later approvals without checking.
- BJ silent first use.
- Full-health check-in quick, no destruction.
- Respawn initially intended dispensing-only.

Timing:

- Target 5.5 seconds full sequence.
- **Hard maximum 7 seconds**, not 20.
- Repeat sequence skippable.
- Initial respawn target <=2 sec; full-health <=0.5 sec.
- Pause threats, input guard, post-release protection, no immediate retrigger.

All five teams were explicitly assigned work. Engineering integrates last after Art/Audio/Mechanics. Marketing half-page writeup.

**Later gameplay change recorded in storybook chapter 51:** one midpoint checkpoint with **one spare of selected hero**, first replacement empties cabinet for rest of run, later respawns occur without further dispense; three lives unchanged. This supersedes assumptions of unlimited stocked replacements. Verify live rules.

**Later art direction:**

- Rusty vending cabinet.
- Glass front.
- Sleeping copies of whichever hero selected, not mixed Tony/Sean.
- Later one-spare change means check current art/mechanics rather than insisting on initial “couple of clones.”
- Art delivered illustrations/sleeping sprites before runtime cabinet layers; missing layers were identified as dropped handoff and Engineering combined around build 48.

Files include:

- `scripts/employee_dispenser.gd`
- `assets/world/spare-employee-dispenser/`
- `handoffs/marketing-discussion-game-intent-audit.json`
- `handoffs/game-intent-story-review.json`
- `marketing/magazine/dispenser-copy-handoff.json`

### Dispenser public copy restriction

Sean rejected **all overt explanation** in magazine of what happens: killing, squishing, fresh healed hero, keeping existing shape, processing twice, etc. Never mention viewer screen/fourth-wall effect in magazine. Imply disturbing corporate practice through euphemism and omissions. This does **not** remove approved game animation.

Separate proposed copy handoff, not applied by Storyboarding:

`marketing/magazine/dispenser-copy-handoff.json`

Feature heading: “Mainframe has made arrangements.”

Column 1, 70 words:

> Mainframe Plumbing & Supply would like you to know that arrangements have been made. The Spare Employee Dispenser stands ready between service calls, its glass front offering a reassuring view of the company’s preparations. There is rust around the hinges and something familiar about the occupants. The accompanying leaflet describes them as reserve personnel. It asks employees to respect their rest and directs all further questions to the same leaflet.

Column 2, 71 words:

> The leaflet is particularly clear on continuity of service. Your assignments will remain on the schedule, your tools will still be required, and your name will stay on the rota. Several paragraphs explain how much the company values an experienced employee. The section headed “What this means for you” refers back to those paragraphs. We would have preferred a little more detail, but the cabinet does appear to be well stocked.

Ad headline: “We have your next shift covered.”
Cover teaser: “Your position is secure.”
Caption: “The company asks that reserve personnel not be disturbed.”

Leaflet is creative framing, not committed collectible or mechanic. Marketing was asked to hold PDF regeneration while Sean supplied feedback. Later editions advanced; check latest hold, don’t assume permanent global ban or permission to publish now.

## Magazine editorial rules and source

Current canonical editable source:

`marketing/magazine/magazine.json`

Builder:

`marketing/magazine/build_guide.py`

Earlier all copy was hardcoded in Python; Sean requested plain-text editable source. I asked Marketing to make JSON authoritative for **all** prose, captions, headings, credits, metadata, image references/layout settings; Python drawing logic only. Source exists now. Verify README/build instructions.

Publication directory:

`marketing/magazine/`

Historical PDFs retain previous names/editions. Do not rewrite archives.

Editorial voice:

- Experienced trade-magazine editor covering absurd conditions.
- Respect trade and hero competence; warm toward crew, dry toward management.
- Not internal design document.
- No development jargon: sprite sheets, atlases, source frames, runtime, integration, collision, frame alignment, implementation reports, agent TODOs.
- Reader loves games but has no technical background assumed.
- Player concepts like health, checkpoint, reload are okay.
